diagnosis: In `_constrained_ltr_repair`, `st.remaining_tokens = length - len(prefix)` shrinks every step. For a DSL-native (lexer) tokenizer, `exact_forced_token_id` only asked `build_completion_forest` for a *complete* terminal witness reaching EOS within that budget. When the budget was too small to enumerate a witness (`_openui_completion_domain` in `src/slm_training/dsl/pack.py` returning `status="incomplete", reason="terminal_witness_unavailable"`), the proof was discarded even when the structural completion forest (`_build_openui_completion_forest`, budget-independent) had already proven exactly one legal next action. `CompletionForest.coverage` collapsed both cases -- 'no witness within horizon' and 'witness disagrees/contradictory' -- to the same value "none", so `exact_forced_token_id` returned None and the repair loop ran an avoidable forward.

fix.summary: Distinguish 'no witness within horizon' from 'witness disagrees' in CompletionForest.coverage, and let a sole-legal structural proof stand on its own when only the terminal-witness search is horizon-limited.

changes.change: _openui_completion_domain: when the witnessed-candidates loop finds zero witnesses within budget AND the structural forest (`initial.paths`, computed independent of budget) has exactly one legal action, return status="partial" with that single action as the sole candidate (empty terminal_witness) and reason="terminal_witness_horizon_limited". Zero or more-than-one structural paths still return status="incomplete"/reason="terminal_witness_unavailable" (contradictory or genuinely ambiguous -- unchanged, fails closed).

build_completion_forest maps domain.status "partial" to CompletionForest.coverage="partial" (carrying the domain's one candidate); only UnsupportedCapabilityV1 or a status outside {"complete","partial"} collapses to coverage="none".
exact_forced_token_id (DSL-native branch): accepts forest.coverage in ("complete", "partial") when exactly one candidate id is present, instead of requiring strictly "complete".

fix.blast_radius: Every other consumer of CompletionForest.coverage (src/slm_training/dsl/grammar/fastpath/speculative_rank.py, src/slm_training/dsl/solver/decode.py, src/slm_training/models/onnx_inference.py, src/slm_training/models/twotower.py forward-admission checks, src/slm_training/models/grammar.py pick_constrained_token._compiler_admits) still requires coverage=="complete" verbatim and therefore still fails closed (forwards/rejects) on "partial" exactly as it already did on "none". Only exact_forced_token_id's DSL-native bypass check was widened.

target_test_before.failure: AssertionError: forwarded, raised from the monkeypatched _denoiser_forward at tests/test_models/test_inference_speed.py:645, propagating out of _constrained_ltr_repair (src/slm_training/models/twotower.py:4525) because exact_forced_token_id returned None (build_completion_forest coverage="none" at remaining_tokens=1).

singleton_probe.description: build_completion_forest on the SAMPLE row's 'root' prefix (output_tokenizer="lexer"), which has exactly one legal next lexeme ('='), at several decode-horizon budgets.
singleton_probe.note: coverage stays "partial" even at remaining_tokens=8 for this grammar because the full Card(":t.x") terminal witness needs more than 8 tokens to reach EOS -- exactly the horizon-limited case I2 names. The fix forces the single legal next token regardless; it never claims full-witness completeness.

ambiguity_control_probe.description: build_completion_forest on the SAMPLE row's 'root =' prefix, which has 19-40 legal next component choices, at the same small budgets -- proves the fix does not widen the bypass to genuinely ambiguous positions.
ambiguity_control_probe.note: unchanged from pre-fix behavior: coverage="none" at small budgets here because 0 or >1 structural paths exist, so exact_forced_token_id still returns None and a forward still runs. This is the 'witness disagrees'/contradictory case the doc says must keep failing closed.

invariant_compliance: Not a legality violation: the forced token was already the unique legal continuation under the DFA/compiler-forest proof before this change; only the (over-strict) requirement to also prove full termination-reachability within the current truncated budget is relaxed. Certainty is never downgraded into a soft preference -- the ambiguity_control_probe shows genuinely non-singleton positions still fail closed.
post_review_fix: Per PR #889 review: _openui_completion_domain's horizon-limited singleton branch now also requires len(tokens) <= budget before returning "partial" (previously unguarded), so a sole structural action that itself does not fit the remaining decode budget still falls through to the existing "incomplete" fail-closed path instead of forcing a token beyond the horizon. Re-verified: target test and full test_inference_speed.py/test_onnx_inference.py suites still pass after the guard (the regression case has len(tokens)=1 <= budget=1).
